preconditions.description: Number of test cases is between 1 and 10.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= H <= 1000 and 1 <= W <= 1000 for H, W in zip(Hs, Ws))
preconditions.description: Each grid has dimensions between 1 and 1000.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= N <= 200 for N in Ns)
preconditions.description: Number of particles is between 1 and 200.

preconditions.expression: all(-1000 <= h[i][j] <= 1000 for i in range(H) for j in range(W) for h in hs)
preconditions.description: Grid cell values are between -1000 and 1000.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= y[i] <= H and 1 <= x[i] <= W for i in range(N) for y, x in zip(ys, xs))
preconditions.description: Particle positions are within the grid dimensions.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= abs_p[i] <= 100 for i in range(N) for abs_p in abs_ps)
preconditions.description: Absolute particle values are between 1 and 100.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set(zip(y, x))) == N for y, x in zip(ys, xs))
preconditions.description: No two particles are in the same cell.

postconditions.description: There are exactly two lines of output for each test case.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer.

postconditions.expression: all(all(sign in ['1', '-1'] for sign in stdout_lines[2*i+1].split()) for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: The second line of each test case contains N space-separated integers, each being either '1' or '-1'.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout_lines[2*i+1].split()) == Ns[i] for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: The number of signs in the second line matches the number of particles.
